note: Full-pipeline pairs bootstrap (B=500, ridge + content-keyed fixed-pooled-PC1 estimator, same procedure as results/replications/baur_bootstrap_check.json for boston/nyc/sf) extended to chicago and philadelphia, the two highest-leverage markets. Produced via baur_pooled_pca.py --city {chicago,philadelphia} --fast --n_boot 500 --pooled_csv results/replications/pooled_pca_treatment_keyed.csv, BOOSTER_NJOBS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, seed=42. theta/CI signs are raw (unoriented), matching the sign convention of baur_bootstrap_check.json.
interpretation: Both chicago and philadelphia show the bootstrap CI essentially coincident with the influence-function CI (chicago: boot width 0.0734 vs IF width 0.0733, +0.1%; philadelphia: boot width 0.0324 vs IF width 0.0362, -10.4%, i.e. the bootstrap is somewhat narrower, same direction and similar magnitude as the -11% seen for nyc). Both CIs exclude zero with wide margin in both markets under either method -- the full-pipeline resample confirms the IF-SE headline is not an artifact of generated-regressor variance being understated for these two high-effect cities.
